roadmapTask: Add a read-only getTabState action to the chrome-bridge MCP that reports the dedicated sandbox tab and the currently-focused active tab of the sandbox tab's window (each with id/url/title plus a sandboxTabActive flag), so an external MCP client can independently verify background-tab capture without trusting the human's word.

phases.gateRun: cd tools/chrome-bridge && npm run verify (tsc --noEmit, eslint . --max-warnings 0, vitest run=254 passed)

dimensionScores.evidence: TabIdentity is exported with exactly { id: number; url: string; title: string }, all readonly, no windowId/optional flags; both readTab and activeTabOfWindow return TabIdentityWithWindow = TabIdentity & { windowId: number } rather than an inline duplicate; both fakePorts literals are typed (page-actions uses explicit Promise<TabIdentityWithWindow> annotations, service-worker infers via the ChromePorts return) with no cast. 9 because all passCriteria are met cleanly; a 10 would need an additional strictly-cleaner contract refinement (e.g. moving TabIdentityWithWindow into protocol/types.ts so the protocol owns the window-augmented shape too), which I cannot point to as a concrete improvement — the intersection is explicitly sanctioned by passCriteria #2.

readTab is `tabIdentity(await chrome.tabs.get(tabId))` — a bare await with no try/catch, no .catch, so a chrome.tabs.get rejection propagates verbatim; ports.unit.test.ts proves it with the 'propagates a rejection' case asserting the exact 'No tab with id: 99.' message flows out unreconstructed. url/title come from `tab.url ?? ""` / `tab.title ?? ""`, so the result type is string, never string | undefined. This is a faithful mirror of chrome.tabs.get including rejection — the concrete 10 property: zero interception of the rejection plus a proving test.

activeTabOfWindow(windowId) is `chrome.tabs.query({ active: true, windowId })` with the only parameter being windowId; no chrome.windows.getCurrent/getLastFocused, no currentWindow key, no fallback to focused window, and empty array resolves to undefined (not a fabricated placeholder). ports.unit.test.ts asserts the query received exactly `{ active: true, windowId: 11 }` and that the empty case resolves toBeUndefined. 9: correct strict plumb-through with all passCriteria met; a 10 would additionally assert the QueryInfo carries only the windowId key and no default-scoping key even in the literal.

git diff confirms queryActiveTab is byte-for-byte unchanged — signature stays `queryActiveTab(): Promise<ActiveTab | undefined>` and the body still uses `chrome.tabs.query({ active: true, currentWindow: true })` resolving from the current window; the only diff hunks are pure additions. There are exactly two reads (one current-window active-tab read, one window-parameterized read) — not collapsed into a shared getActiveTab({ windowId? }) helper.

Both fakePorts() literals implement readTab and activeTabOfWindow: page-actions.unit.test.ts (explicit Promise<TabIdentityWithWindow> return) and service-worker.unit.test.ts (inferred via ChromePorts), each returning stable { id, windowId, url, title } identities — no rejected/empty stubs. `npx tsc --noEmit` in tools/chrome-bridge exits 0, and a grep across all four touched files finds zero `@ts-ignore`/`@ts-expect-error`/`as unknown as` annotations.

phases.liveVerdict: VERIFIED via real chrome-bridge MCP session (Chrome Bridge extension loaded unpacked from tools/chrome-bridge/dist/extension, freshly remove+re-added; relay ws://127.0.0.1:8766). getTabState advertised + returns the {sandboxTab, activeTab, sandboxTabActive} shape. Focus-flip round trip demonstrated with manual browser tab clicks (labeled): (1) focused tab = chrome://extensions (id 1799002408): sandboxTab={id:1799003886,url:https://www.linkedin.com/feed/,title:Feed | LinkedIn}, activeTab!=sandbox, sandboxTabActive=false. (2) focused the LinkedIn sandbox tab (human click): sandboxTabActive=true, activeTab={id:1799003886} (id equality). (3) focused a Google Search tab (id 1799001612) in the same window: sandboxTabActive=false, activeTab={id:1799001612, Google search} (identity changed). (4) captureTab after the flip still returns a PNG screenshot of the backgrounded LinkedIn sandbox tab. No active-tab-as-target path (handler calls only readTab/activeTabOfWindow/peekStoredSandboxTabId). Environ note: example.com DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN in sandbox (network quirk, not a bridge issue); sandbox tab then navigated to linkedin.com which loaded and was screenshotted. Horizon is ready to close VERIFIED.
